name: Azariah
overview: Azariah was a male figure known as the son of Hoshaiah who opposed the prophet Jeremiah, as recorded in Jeremiah 43:2. Beyond this opposition, little else is noted about his tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His mention is brief but significant within the context of Jeremiah's ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Azariah means 'YHWH has helped,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew proper name. This meaning underscores the reliance on God's assistance, although the name itself was not given directly by God according to the record in Jeremiah 43:2.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Azariah as the son of Hoshaiah in Jeremiah 43:2. No other familial relationships are recorded for him beyond this father-son connection.
scriptureSignificance: Azariah's significance lies in his opposition to Jeremiah, illustrating the resistance the prophet faced during his mission. This opposition highlights the challenges to God's message during a critical period in Judah's history. His identity as Hoshaiah's son situates him within the social context of Jeremiah's time, emphasizing the personal and communal tensions surrounding the prophetic word.
